Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Lisa Wong, CTO; and David Kim, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results may differ materially due to various risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of these factors.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm thrilled to report on CloudForge's outstanding performance in Q2 fiscal 2024. We hit significant milestones this quarter, propelled by robust demand for our ForgeAI platform and flawless execution across our strategic priorities.

Our focus this quarter centered on five critical areas: evolving our customer mix toward higher-value enterprise accounts, enhancing sales efficiency through shorter cycles and better conversions, optimizing customer acquisition costs, maintaining disciplined operating expenses, and accelerating new customer wins to boost ARR and MRR.

These efforts have positioned us stronger than ever, with enterprise momentum building rapidly and our AI innovations resonating deeply with customers. We're confident in sustaining this trajectory to create enduring value for shareholders.

Now, I'll hand it over to Mike Patel to walk through the financials and expand on these areas.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah highlighted, we delivered a powerhouse quarter. Total revenue reached $168 million, up 28% year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 82%, reflecting our continued operational leverage, while non-GAAP operating income came in at $24 million.

Turning first to our customer mix, which remains a cornerstone of our high-quality, predictable revenue stream. We categorize customers into enterprise—those with over 1,000 employees or more than $500 million in annual revenue—and SMB for the balance. This split provides sharp insights into our go-to-market performance and scalability potential.

The top line here: enterprise now accounts for 62% of total ARR, a jump from 55% last year and 48% two years ago. SMB has accordingly shifted to 38%, down from 45% and 52%. This isn't a pivot away from SMB—we still value its role—but rather the result of our effective land-and-expand strategy in enterprise, where new logos average over $250,000 ACV versus $12,000 for SMB. In Q2, enterprise drove 72% of new ARR additions, including major expansions with a leading fintech comparable to Stripe and a retailer on par with Shopify's footprint.

Enterprise ARR surged 38% year-over-year in fiscal 2024, far exceeding SMB's steady 16% growth. Key enablers include our enterprise-focused tech stack: federated multi-tenant design with zero-trust security, HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II certifications, and seamless ties to Snowflake and Databricks. We've introduced AI-driven workflow automation akin to UiPath or Celonis, allowing large-scale process orchestration. This has yielded 142% net revenue retention in enterprise, with expansions comprising 28% of total remaining performance obligations, compared to 112% NRR and 8% expansions in SMB.

Geographically, North America, at 68% of enterprise ARR, saw 15 deals exceeding $1 million ACV over the past year, focused on financial services and healthcare—like compliance automation for Dodd-Frank or claims processing for Medicare Advantage payers. EMEA enterprise ARR grew 45% year-over-year, aided by GDPR data sovereignty tools and DAX 40 wins, despite some UK SMB churn rising to 8% annualized. APAC shines for SMB at 22% growth via AWS Marketplace and Alibaba Cloud self-serve, though enterprise is only 25% of regional ARR—we're ramping localized teams for Nikkei 225 targets.

This trajectory echoes Snowflake and ServiceNow's enterprise shift, bringing pricing leverage, reduced churn, and over 120% dollar-based net expansion. Our approach: SMB for product validation, then enterprise via top-down sales and co-sells with Salesforce and Microsoft. Highlights include the Enterprise Success Program lifting premium module adoption like Advanced Analytics by 35%, and 80% fintech POC close rates under 90 days.

We project enterprise at 68-70% of ARR by fiscal 2025 close, backed by a $2.5 billion pipeline at 3.2 times Q4 bookings guidance. SMB fuels innovation and expansion, targeting 25-30% overall ARR growth. This mix ensures resilience, HubSpot-style, through macro turbulence.

Next, sales efficiency, spotlighting cycle lengths and conversion rates—standouts in Q2 amid SaaS peers like Salesforce, Workday, and Snowflake. These metrics bolster our magic number, CAC payback, and Rule of 40 score of 48%.

Sales cycles from MQL to close-won shortened to 92 days, down 18% year-over-year from 112 and 7% quarter-over-quarter from 99—impressive for enterprise complexity with POCs and approvals.

By segment: enterprise over $250K ACV at 145 days, 22% shorter year-over-year, thanks to our self-serve Enterprise Trial covering 28% of pipeline; a Fortune 500 logistics win mirrored ServiceNow speed with two-week POCs via no-code AI. Mid-market $50K-$250K at 68 days, 15% faster, via targeted outbound with Apollo.io and LinkedIn. SMB/self-serve under $50K at 32 days, with tripled volume from PLG like early Slack.

North America averaged 85 days (75% of bookings), boosted by 40% field sales growth in Austin and Boston. EMEA hit 105 days from 130, via localized GDPR features. APAC at 120 days, but Gong coaching pilots aim for 20-25 day cuts by Q4.

Enablers: AI Sales Copilot on Anthropic Claude automates 65% of demos and objections, cutting rep ramps 30%; 6sense intent data boosts qualified opps 40%; refined land-and-expand with 35% Q2 expansions from Q1 pilots.

Conversions: MQL-to-close-won at 14.2%, up 250 basis points year-over-year from 11.7% and 80 bps quarter-over-quarter, generating $28 million new ARR from 2,100 MQLs.

Funnel: MQL-to-SQL 32% (+4 points, 6sense and Terminus); SQL-to-opportunity 68% (+3 points, 120 inside reps and ABM); opportunity-to-close 31% (+5 points, Zoom/Outreach plans, 42% win rate vs. UiPath/SAP). Overall 14.2%. Enterprise net new logos 22% (from 17%), expansions 78% via usage pricing and 150% NRR self-upgrades.

Our bowtie model—PLG for 45% new ARR, success pods for 55% expansions—outshines amid 12% industry slippage. ForgeAI procure-to-pay yields 4x ROI.

We see cycles to 83 days H2, conversions to 16%, CAC payback 14 months, ample for $50 million sales adds toward $450 million ARR.

Shifting to CAC trends: ours blend enterprise sales with PLG, optimizing in a tough macro pressuring Salesforce and HubSpot. Q2 blended CAC at $428 per new customer, 18% better sequentially from $520, 29% down year-over-year from $602—top-quartile per Bessemer, with 118% net expansion and 4.8x LTV/CAC.

By segment: SMB/mid under $100K at $185, down 22% quarter, 35% year-over-year; PLG freemium at 28% conversion (from 19%), 62% self-serve, 4.2-month payback vs. industry 7-9. Enterprise over $100K at $14,200, 12% quarter improvement, 21% year-over-year; 47 Fortune 1000 deals, $285K average ACV up 14%.

Regions: North America $410 (lowest, organic leads up 15%, AWS/Google marketplaces 22% logos); EMEA $495 from $680, GDPR and 12 VARs 3x ROI; APAC $580 down 14%, Tencent localization, Japan/Australia 65% adds.

Drivers: PLG with ML viral prediction (1.3x coefficient), 40% bottom-up pipeline; sales overhaul with 6sense reducing bad leads 31%, MEDDPICC ramps at 2.5 months, AI forecasting; LinkedIn ROAS 5.2x, ABM 2.5x wins; AI must-haves like sales sentiment.

Q3 CAC $400-$420, payback 5.8 months, $25 million sales invest for 25% logos sans margin hit; 28-30% non-GAAP margin.

On operating expenses: total non-GAAP opex $128 million, up 22% year-over-year but down 200 basis points to 76% of revenue—leveraging toward Rule of 40 at 42 (28% growth, 14% margin).

R&D $52 million or 31% revenue, up 32% from $39 million; fueling ForgeAI Agents for autonomous workflows with Pinecone RAG like OpenAI/Anthropic, GPU ML for petabyte data Snowflake-style. Headcount to 450 engineers, 25% growth, 40% Bangalore/Lviv for cost efficiency; APAC for PIPL/DPDP. To moderate to 28-30%, lifting NRR over 120%.

Sales & Marketing $52 million, flat quarter-over-quarter, up 18% year-over-year at 31% revenue (from 35%), targeting under 25%; 14-month payback, 4.2x LTV/CAC. 60% demand gen high-ROI: Google/AWS 3x, ABM for CISOs zero-ETL like Fivetran. EMEA cycles 7 months, APAC bookings +35%; sales to 350, +20% productivity via RevOps AI. Mid-teens growth FY24 for 30% ARR.

G&A $24 million, 14% revenue, up 15%; $8 million SBC at 2.5% dilution, SOX/TSE prep. 25% offshore Manila/Krakow saves 20%; bad debt 0.5% on 98% collections, 115% NRR.

This profile primes 20%+ FCF margins FY25.

Finally, new customer acquisition: we added 452 net new customers, up 28% from 353 last year; total over 4,200, +22%.

Enterprise: 18 new, from 12; three $1M+ ACVs, $8.2 million new ARR at $456K average—record. Commercial: 434, +30%, $3.8 million new ARR at $8.7K, 128% expansion.

Total $12 million new ARR (+32%), $1.02 million new MRR—strongest since Q4 FY22, beating 25% industry. Ex-ForgeAI Guardrails (15% attach), +26%.

Regions: NA 308 (68%, $8.4M, AWS/Snowflake); EMEA 92 (+45%, $2.3M, GDPR); APAC 52 (+22%, $1.3M, Japan ramp).

PLG freemium 14% conversion; ForgeAI shortens cycles 18 days; Gong lead scoring 2.5x velocity, CAC flat $28K.

Q3 $48-52 million new ARR, 500+ logos, enterprise pipeline +35% QoQ.

We keep investing in R&D for innovation and product expansion. Cash stands at $450 million, enabling acquisitions and growth plays.

Updating full-year guidance: revenue now $680 million to $700 million, reflecting first-half strength.

Now, over to Lisa for tech updates.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Mike. In Q2, we advanced our AI stack deeply into the core platform. Adoption of ForgeAI Agents and multimodal features is soaring, boosting engagement and outcomes. We've hardened security with zero-trust and scalability for enterprise scale, including petabyte handling and real-time RAG—meeting hyperscaler demands head-on.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs.

John Doe:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, and what kind of attach rates are you seeing with it?

David Kim:
Thanks, John. ForgeAI has been transformative, contributing over 25% of Q2 new ARR through its workflow automation and anomaly detection. It's shortened enterprise sales cycles by 18 days on average and driven freemium conversions to 28% in SMB. Attach rates are strong at 35% for new logos, rising to 52% in expansions—especially Guardrails at 15% standalone. This mirrors Snowflake's consumption wins, fueling our 128% NRR in commercial and positioning us for 30%+ growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Emily. APAC is a priority, currently 10% of ARR but with huge potential. We've localized pricing, integrated with Tencent and Alibaba Cloud, and added sales teams targeting Nikkei 225 and ASX firms. Q2 saw 22% SMB growth and 52 new logos; enterprise penetration at 25% will rise with data sovereignty features under PIPL/DPDP. Partnerships like AWS Marketplace drive self-serve, and we're investing $10 million in Japan/Australia headcount for 40% H2 growth, building on EMEA's 45% success.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Bob Wilson with JPMorgan.

Bob Wilson:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, and what's the trend you are seeing in NRR?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Bob. Churn is well-contained at 5% annualized overall—enterprise under 4%, SMB at 7%—despite macro pressures. Strategies include our Enterprise Success Program boosting module adoption 35%, AI upsell prompts hitting 78% conversion, and vertical POCs closing 80%. NRR trends up to 118% blended, 142% enterprise, 112-128% commercial/segment—driven by expansions at 28% RPO share. UK SMB ticked to 8%, but collections at 98% and ROI proofs keep us resilient, targeting 120%+.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We're excited about Q2 progress and steadfast in delivering robust shareholder returns. Looking forward to our next call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
